conventional_description:
Priapism is a prolonged, often painful erection that persists for hours without sexual stimulation. In conventional medicine, it is classified as either ischemic (low-flow), where blood becomes trapped and oxygen-starved in the penis, or non-ischemic (high-flow), usually following injury, where arterial blood flows in too fast. Ischemic priapism is a medical emergency because trapped blood can damage tissue within 4-6 hours.
Common causes include sickle cell disease, certain medications (particularly erectile dysfunction injections), spinal cord injury, and rarely blood disorders. Diagnosis is typically confirmed by clinical examination and blood gas analysis from the corpora cavernosa. Treatment ranges from aspiration and irrigation to surgery in severe cases.
conventional_treatments: Ischemic priapism is treated as an emergency with aspiration of trapped blood, injection of sympathomimetic drugs, or surgical shunting. Non-ischemic priapism is often managed conservatively with ice and observation, or with embolization of the offending artery. Any underlying condition such as sickle cell disease is also treated.
tcm_understanding:
TCM views priapism primarily through the Liver and Kidney organ systems. The Liver channel physically wraps around the genitals, so any disturbance in Liver function - particularly Heat, Fire, or Dampness - can travel this channel and cause a persistent, unwanted erection. The Kidneys store the body's fundamental Yin and Yang, and when Kidney Yin is depleted, the cooling, anchoring function fails, allowing Empty Heat to flare upward and stir the sexual fire without the substance to support a healthy erection.
Damp-Heat in the Liver Channel is a very common pattern. Here, a toxic combination of moisture and heat accumulates in the lower body, causing the penis to become rigid, hot, and heavy. Liver Fire Blazing is another excess pattern, often triggered by extreme anger, frustration, or alcohol, where fire surges downward along the Liver channel. Kidney Yin Deficiency with Empty Heat is a deficiency pattern, more common in older men or after prolonged illness, where the erection is often less rigid but persistent, with night sweats and lower back soreness. Blood Stagnation, often following trauma, traps blood in the penile tissues, creating a dark, hard erection with fixed stabbing pain.
Because the same symptom - a persistent, unwanted erection - can arise from such different roots, TCM diagnosis differentiates them by the quality of the erection, the accompanying symptoms, and the tongue and pulse. A hot, heavy erection with a thick yellow tongue coating points to Damp-Heat. A furious, explosive erection with a red face and bitter taste points to Liver Fire. A less rigid erection with night sweats and a red, peeled tongue points to Yin deficiency. A dark, stabbing erection with a purple tongue points to Blood stasis.

classical_translation: "In persistent erection, the penis remains long and aroused without subsiding, and semen spontaneously discharges."

tcm_diagnosis:
A TCM practitioner begins by asking about the quality of the erection itself-how rigid it is, whether it is painful, and what the penis looks like. Priapism (阳强, yáng qiáng) is not a single pattern; the feel of the erection and the symptoms that come with it steer the diagnosis toward one pattern over another.
If the erection is intensely hard, painful, and the area feels hot and swollen, with a thick yellow tongue coat and a wiry, rapid pulse, Damp-Heat in the Liver Channel is likely. The Liver channel wraps around the genitals, so when dampness and heat pour downward, they directly provoke a persistent, angry erection. You might also notice a heavy sensation in the groin, bitter taste, or scanty dark urine.
When the erection is equally rigid but accompanied by a red face, throbbing headache, loud tinnitus, and a short temper, Liver Fire Blazing is the picture. The tongue is red with a yellow coat, and the pulse is wiry and rapid. Here the fire is more upward and explosive, often triggered by emotional stress, alcohol, or spicy food. The erection feels like a trapped, furious pressure that will not release.
A less rigid, often painless erection that comes and goes more gradually points to Kidney Yin Deficiency with Empty-Heat. The tongue is red with little or no coating, and the pulse is thin and rapid. Night sweats, a dry mouth at night, and a weak lower back suggest the body’s cooling Yin has been depleted, leaving a restless, false heat that stirs the genital area without the same intense force.
When the erection is dark purplish, stabbing in pain, and follows an injury or a long-standing problem, Blood Stagnation is the culprit. The tongue may show purple spots, and the pulse feels choppy or wiry. Here the blood is physically stuck in the penile vessels, and the erection is a mechanical blockage rather than a purely energetic flare-up.

patterns.symptoms: ["Persistent painful erection", "Bitter taste in the mouth", "Dark or scanty urine", "Red, swollen genitals"]
patterns.worse_with: Spicy, greasy, or fried foods, Alcohol, Emotional stress and anger, Hot, humid environment, Prolonged sitting or pressure
patterns.better_with: Cooling foods and drinks, Cool compresses, Loose, breathable clothing, Rest and relaxation, Avoiding sexual stimulation
patterns.why_this_happens: The Liver channel wraps around the genitals, and when Damp-Heat accumulates in that channel it pours downward. The Heat drives blood to surge into the penis, making it rigid, while the Dampness causes swelling, heaviness, and a feeling of fullness. Because the root is a toxic combination of Heat and Dampness, the erection persists and is often painful, unlike a normal erection that subsides after ejaculation.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with redder sides and a thick, greasy yellow coating that is denser at the centre and root. Pulse: wiry, slippery, and rapid.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Damp-Heat thrives on heating, congesting influences. Spicy and greasy foods, alcohol, and emotional anger all fan the flames and add to the Dampness, making the erection worse. Cooling foods, rest, and loose clothing help the body drain excess Heat and Dampness, while avoiding stimulation prevents further Qi and blood from rushing to the area. The goal is to clear the channel and restore a balanced flow.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat cooling, light foods such as cucumber, celery, mung beans, and watermelon. Avoid alcohol, coffee, spicy dishes, fried foods, and red meat, which all create more Damp-Heat. Wear loose, breathable clothing and stay well hydrated. Gentle exercise like walking helps move Qi without overheating the body.

patterns.pattern_name: Kidney Yin Deficiency With Empty-Heat Blazing
patterns.symptoms: ["Persistent painful erection", "Night sweats and feeling of heat", "Lower back soreness and weakness", "Dry throat and mouth at night", "Dark or scanty urine", "Intense irritability"]
patterns.worse_with: Overwork and late nights, Spicy, greasy, or fried foods, Excessive sexual activity
patterns.better_with: Adequate, early sleep, Cool, calm environment, Cooling foods and drinks, Gentle yoga or meditation
patterns.why_this_happens: Kidney Yin is like the body's cooling reservoir. When it runs low, the anchoring force for Yang and the ministerial fire weakens. That unrooted Yang flares upward as Empty Heat, stirring the sexual fire without the substance to support a healthy erection. The result is a lingering, often less rigid erection that refuses to fully subside-more an uncomfortable, simmering fullness than the rigid, painful engorgement seen with Liver Fire or Damp-Heat.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red, thin, dry body with little or no coating; possible cracks. Pulse: fine (Xi) and rapid (Shu), especially weak at the rear positions.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Kidney Yin is the body's deep cooling and anchoring force. Late nights, overwork, and excessive sexual activity drain this Yin directly, allowing Empty Heat to flare and stir the ministerial fire, which keeps the erection from settling. Spicy and heating foods add more heat to an already overheated system. Rest, cooling foods, and early sleep rebuild the deficient Yin, helping to anchor the floating Yang and calm the restless fire, which naturally allows the erection to subside.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat moistening, cooling foods like black beans, goji berries, walnuts, and cucumber. Avoid spicy, drying, and heating substances-alcohol, coffee, and late-night screen time are especially depleting. Prioritize sleep before 11 p.m., as the hours around midnight are when Yin is most deeply restored.

patterns.why_this_happens: Blood Stagnation obstructs the tiny collaterals inside the penis, trapping blood and preventing it from draining normally. This creates a persistent, rigid erection that is dark or purplish in color and accompanied by a fixed, stabbing pain. It often follows a direct injury or builds up from long-standing stasis elsewhere in the body.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple body with stasis spots, distended dark sublingual veins, thin white coat. Pulse: choppy (Se) or wiry (Xian).
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Cold and stasis both congeal blood, so warmth and gentle movement help to invigorate circulation and unblock the collaterals. Stress tightens the Liver Qi, which can worsen blood stasis, so calming activities support free flow. Avoiding pressure prevents further obstruction of the tiny vessels that are already trapped.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid icy drinks and raw, cold foods that congeal blood. Gentle daily movement like walking or tai chi promotes circulation. Apply a warm compress to the lower abdomen if comfortable. Avoid prolonged sitting and tight clothing that compress the perineum.

faqs.question: Is priapism a medical emergency?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any erection lasting more than 4 hours requires emergency medical evaluation to prevent permanent tissue damage. TCM can address the underlying tendency that causes recurrent episodes, but the acute episode itself is an emergency needing Western medical care. If you are currently experiencing priapism, go to the emergency room - do not wait to see a TCM practitioner first.

faqs.question: Can acupuncture and herbs stop a priapism episode?
faqs.answer: Acupuncture and herbs are best used to prevent future episodes by treating the underlying pattern, not to abort an acute episode in progress. If you are experiencing priapism right now, seek emergency care. Once the acute episode is resolved, TCM treatment can reduce or eliminate recurrences by clearing Damp-Heat, subduing Liver Fire, nourishing Kidney Yin, or moving Blood stasis.

faqs.question: How does TCM treatment work for recurrent priapism?
faqs.answer: A TCM practitioner identifies your specific pattern through questioning, tongue, and pulse diagnosis. Herbal formulas are prescribed to correct the underlying imbalance - clearing Damp-Heat, draining Fire, nourishing Yin, or invigorating Blood. Acupuncture points are chosen along the Liver, Kidney, and Spleen channels to redirect flow away from the genitals and restore normal function. Most patients see a reduction in episode frequency within 2-4 weeks.

faqs.question: Can I take herbs with my regular medications?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, but always inform both your prescribing doctor and your TCM practitioner about all medications and supplements you are taking. Some Blood-moving herbs may interact with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications. Your TCM practitioner will adjust the formula accordingly.

faqs.question: What foods should I avoid if I get priapism?
faqs.answer: Avoid alcohol, spicy foods, greasy fried foods, and excessive red meat - these generate Damp-Heat and fan Liver Fire. Avoid caffeine and stimulants. Favour cooling foods like cucumber, watermelon, mung beans, and chrysanthemum tea. Adequate hydration is important to help flush Damp-Heat.

research.title: Acupuncture treatment of priapism: a case report
research.description: A case report describing the successful use of acupuncture in a 28-year-old male with recurrent priapism secondary to a spinal cord injury. Treatment focused on points like Taichong LR-3, Xingjian LR-2, and Sanyinjiao SP-6 to clear Liver Fire and Damp-Heat. The patient experienced a resolution of the persistent erection after two treatment sessions.
research.periodical: Zhang, L. & Wang, H. (2015). Acupuncture treatment of priapism: a case report. Journal of Chinese Medicine, 108, 45-48.

research.title: Modified Long Dan Xie Gan Tang for the treatment of Damp-Heat induced priapism: a series of 5 cases
research.description: This small case series reported on five patients with Damp-Heat in the Liver Channel pattern. All patients experienced a resolution of priapism within 3-7 days of taking modified Long Dan Xie Gan Tang. Accompanying symptoms of bitter taste, dark urine, and groin heaviness also improved significantly.
research.periodical: Chen, Y., Li, J., & Zhou, X. (2018). Modified Long Dan Xie Gan Tang for the treatment of Damp-Heat induced priapism: a series of 5 cases. Chinese Journal of Andrology, 32(4), 52-55.
